newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan sees no sharp rise in exports to US.
newsitem.headline: Nissan sees no sharp rise in exports to US.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Monday it had no plans to sharply increase its exports to the United States.

Asked about calls for Japan to reduce its trade surplus at the G7 summit, Nissan president Yoshikazu Hanawa said: "We have a company policy of using exports to cover one-third of demand (in the United States) while the rest is covered locally."
He said at that level, he does not expect the company to sharply increase its exports to the United States.
Tadao Takei, an executive vice president in charge of domestic sales at Nissan Motor, said the company expects steady domestic sales in July from year-ago levels.
Hanawa said Nissan, a major client of failed Nissan Mutual Life Insurance, said it may take on some staff from the failed insurer and was ready to accept a cut in guaranteed returns on its policies.
